notes: No separate `test` skill: a CI workflow file has no independent test suite of its own beyond the platform linter (actionlint / GitLab CI Lint), which `ci-pipeline-implementation`'s own Verify step and `ci-pipeline-build-fix` already cover -- a dedicated `test` skill would duplicate one of those two rather than earn a distinct place. No `migrate` skill: migrating GitHub Actions runtime/syntax versions or GitLab CI schema changes did not reach the bar for a distinct skill in this pass (unlike `ts-js-node`/`react`'s ESM/version-upgrade migrations, there is no single recurring migration shape specific enough to write a focused skill and eval suite around yet) -- left for a future batch if a concrete need shows up.

auditFocus: a pull_request_target job that checks out github.event.pull_request.head.sha/.ref and then runs a build/test/lint step against it (the pwn-request pattern)
a third-party uses: action pinned to a mutable tag (@v4, @main) instead of a full commit SHA
a workflow-level permissions: write-all, or no permissions: block at all, on a workflow whose jobs do not all need write access
${{ github.event.* }} or an untrusted CI/CD variable interpolated directly into a run:/script: shell string instead of passed through env:/variables: first
a GitLab CI deploy job consuming a Protected+Masked variable with no rules: restricting it to the protected branch/tag that variable is exposed to
a cache key that never changes, or a job with no timeout-minutes/timeout on a step that can hang
buildCommands: actionlint (GitHub Actions workflow files, when configured)
the project's own GitLab CI Lint / gitlab-ci-lint run (.gitlab-ci.yml, when configured)
re-trigger the specific failing run to confirm the named error is resolved
fixGuardrails: never grant a broader permissions: scope than the specific failing step needs, and never at the workflow level to fix one job's failure
never unprotect a GitLab CI/CD variable, or remove a rules:/branch gate protecting it, just to make a job on the wrong branch pass
never disable or loosen a rules:/if: condition to make a job "just run" without understanding why it was scoped that way
never pin an action to a tag to work around a SHA-pinning lint failure instead of resolving to the correct commit SHA
